newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Key Australia senator links Telstra with jobs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Key Australia senator links Telstra with jobs.

text.p: Australian independent senator Mal Colston said his vote on the partial sale of telecommunications group Telstra Corp was dependent on an agreement from the government to protect jobs in rural areas.
"I am not sure about an offer to be made to me, something that would take my concerns away perhaps," Colston told Australian Broadcasting Corp Radio on Friday.

"But if I don't have something like that my support wouldn't be there," Colston said. He said he would need an "iron clad" agreement from the Liberal-National government to assure him Telstra job losses would not occur in rural areas.
"There would have to be something in the legislation or something similar to make sure Telstra job losses do not occur in the rural areas," Colston said.
The government plans to raise A$8 billion from the one-third sale of Telstra with A$1 billion of that earmarked for its environmental upgrade programme.

Colston and fellow independent senator Brian Harradine are crucial to the passage of the Telstra legislation as the government needs two extra votes to pass any legislation in the Senate. The non-government parties are opposed to the sale.
